---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Irreversible Commitment Gap At Own-History Extreme
EXPRESSION: TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(capx, COALESCE(aqc, 0)), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm is most exposed when its total sunk commitment — capital expenditure plus acquisition spending, net of flexible research spending — sits at the top of its own five-year range, because that is the point at which the firm has locked in the most irreversible capital it has ever carried relative to its revenue base.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Gen 7 produced two independent improvements on the champion reallocation idea, the own-history state formulation (fmb -5.71, alpha -4.8%, Sharpe -0.82) and the inclusion of acquisitions in the hard budget (fmb -4.81), and this is the one specification that tests whether they are complementary rather than substitutes. Because TS_RANK benchmarks each firm against itself, the lumpiness of acquisition spending that threatened the flow version is absorbed into the firm's own history rather than creating cross-sectional tail outliers.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Hard Tilt State Deflated By Capital Base
EXPRESSION: TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ppent, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: The hard-versus-soft spending gap is best scaled by the capital base it is reshaping — plant plus accumulated knowledge — rather than by revenue, because the capital deflator removes the margin and turnover heterogeneity that revenue scaling embeds.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Both deflators have now been validated on the flow version of the reallocation measure, with the capital-base deflator producing the larger alpha (-5.0%, t -5.27) and the revenue deflator the larger slope, so resolving the deflator choice inside the stronger own-history state formulation is the single most informative remaining design test in this family. The denominator is strictly positive and slow-moving, so the within-firm ranking reflects the numerator's reallocation content rather than denominator noise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Soft Tilt State With Profit Growth
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5))), RANK(GROWTH(SUB(sale, cogs), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm whose spending gap has moved to the knowledge-tilted end of its own five-year history while its gross profit is still growing is deliberately funding innovation out of a healthy business, not rationing capital under distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Funded Research Tilt With Profit Delivery was the strongest long-side result ever recorded here (fmb 5.15, alpha +4.9%, t 4.99), and the parallel short-side evidence says the own-history state dominates the one-year flow difference, so substituting the state for the flow in the long-side construct is the natural consolidation and it holds the profit-delivery screen fixed for a clean comparison. Both legs remain non-negative ranks, so the product stays monotone and the distress cases that would otherwise pollute the knowledge-tilted tail are screened out by the profit requirement.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Hard Tilt State With Profit Decline
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5)), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(SUB(sale, cogs), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Building capacity at the expense of research is most damaging when gross profit is already contracting, because the firm is committing sunk capital to a business whose earning power is visibly deteriorating.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The profit-delivery screen transformed the long side of the reallocation family, and this asks the symmetric question on the short side: whether the champion's -4.8% alpha concentrates in firms whose fundamentals are simultaneously deteriorating, which would identify the mechanism as misallocation under decline rather than generic overinvestment. Together with the previous proposal it decomposes the reallocation spread by profit direction, which is the most valuable remaining diagnostic for interpreting the archive's strongest family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Broad Intangible Budget Including Advertising
EXPRESSION: TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0))), MA(sale, 3)), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: Brand building is intangible investment of the same economic kind as research — expensed, flexible, and value-relevant — so the hard-versus-soft spending gap should be measured against total soft investment rather than research alone.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Advertising has never been usefully tested in this archive because cross-sectional constructions turned it into a consumer-industry reporting indicator, but inside a within-firm TS_RANK the comparison is always the same firm against itself, which is the one setting where the reporting-population problem does not bite. If the broad-soft version matches or beats the research-only champion, the mechanism is about flexibility versus irreversibility of investment generally rather than about research specifically.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Capital Stock Hard Tilt At Own-History Extreme
EXPRESSION: TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, ADD(ppent, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: The accumulated consequence of years of hard-tilted spending is a capital base whose knowledge share has fallen to its own five-year low, and firms in that state carry the most replicable and least defensible asset mix they have ever held.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive has shown the flow reallocation is priced and that its stock analogue in cross-section is also priced but weakly (Capital Composition Drifting Toward Plant, alpha -2.2%), and the missing test is the stock analogue expressed as a within-firm state, which is exactly the transformation that tripled the strength of the flow measure. Because the ratio is bounded and built on slow-moving stocks, the resulting sort should have low turnover and stable portfolio composition, a useful contrast with the flow-based champion's higher-frequency rebalancing.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---CRITIQUE Irreversible Commitment Gap At Own-History Extreme---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A legitimate, if incremental, test of whether the two independently validated gen-7 improvements (own-history state, acquisition-inclusive hard budget) are complementary, and the within-firm ranking is the right construction for lumpy aqc — but it remains a single-term addition to the reigning champion, so a null result would be uninformative and a positive one only marginally so.

---CRITIQUE Hard Tilt State Deflated By Capital Base---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated motivation is internally inconsistent with the expression — TS_RANK already ranks each firm against itself, so cross-firm margin and turnover heterogeneity is removed regardless of deflator, and the deflator only alters within-firm time dynamics (a slow-moving, near-constant capital denominator will leave the within-firm ordering nearly identical to the revenue-deflated champion), making this closer to a cosmetic variant than the "single most informative remaining design test."

---CRITIQUE Soft Tilt State With Profit Growth---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Substituting the stronger own-history state for the one-year flow inside the archive's best long-side construct is a coherent consolidation with the conditioning leg held fixed, though the marginal information over its two well-tested parents is modest and the gross-profit-growth leg risks importing a plain profitability/growth effect.

---CRITIQUE Hard Tilt State With Profit Decline---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Given both legs are [0,1] ranks, this signal equals the previous proposal's signal minus the linear term (profit-growth rank − hard-tilt rank), so it is very largely a sign-flipped restatement of proposal 3 rather than an independent decomposition, and the residual curvature difference is unlikely to justify a separate test.

---CRITIQUE Broad Intangible Budget Including Advertising---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: This is the one proposal that tests a genuinely distinct economic claim — that the mechanism is investment irreversibility generally rather than R&D specifically — and the within-firm framing is a sensible response to xad's reporting-population problem, though COALESCE(xad,0) will still inject spurious within-firm jumps for firms that start or stop disclosing advertising, which should be diagnosed if results shift.

---CRITIQUE Capital Stock Hard Tilt At Own-History Extreme---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The construction is degenerate for the large population of non-R&D reporters, whose ratio is identically 1.0 in every year so that TS_RANK is constant/undefined and piles them at the extreme short leg with zero information content, which will contaminate exactly the portfolio tail the hypothesis depends on.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Hard Tilt Both Absolutely And Relative To Own History
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: The most exposed firms are those whose spending gap is hard-tilted both against their industry-wide peer distribution and against their own five-year history, since a high absolute commitment that is also unusual for the firm identifies a fresh, aggressive shift rather than a stable business model.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The critic's own argument establishes that TS_RANK strips out all cross-firm heterogeneity, which means the champion discards the level information entirely and cannot distinguish a chronically capital-intensive firm at its own peak from a knowledge-heavy firm making the same relative move; adding the cross-sectional rank restores that orthogonal dimension rather than adjusting a deflator that leaves the within-firm ordering nearly unchanged. This is the only way to test whether the two rankings carry complementary information, and SUMRANK keeps both components bounded so neither dominates through outliers.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Externally Funded Hard Tilt State
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: A shift to the firm's most hard-tilted spending posture is far more damaging when it is financed by newly raised outside capital, because internally funded capacity building is disciplined by cash generation while externally funded building is not.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The critic is right that conditioning the hard-tilt state on gross-profit decline is algebraically almost the mirror of conditioning the soft-tilt state on gross-profit growth, so this replaces the profit dimension with an economically independent one — the funding source — which the archive has separately validated (external financing paired with the hard investment mix produced fmb -2.76, alpha -3.2%, Sharpe -0.26). The question it answers is new and sharp: whether the reallocation penalty is an overinvestment story about where money is spent or a financing story about where the money came from.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Plant Stock At Own-History Peak Against Knowledge-Inclusive Scale
EXPRESSION: TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), MA(sale, 3))), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: When a firm's physical capital base reaches its own five-year high relative to the combined scale of its revenue and its accumulated knowledge capital, the accumulated overbuild is at its most extreme and subsequent returns are low.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: The degeneracy the critic identified is removed because the denominator now contains a smoothed revenue term, so the ratio varies through time for firms that report no research and they are ranked on their own genuine capital-intensity history instead of piling at a constant extreme. The construct still tests the stock analogue of the champion — accumulated physical commitment measured against a knowledge-inclusive scale — while retaining the low-turnover, slow-moving portfolio composition that makes it a useful contrast with the flow-based signals.
